# greta.distributions {#sec-greta-distributions}

::: {.callout-note}
## Summary

- **greta.distributions is ready for a first CRAN release.** The
  package checks `0 errors | 0 warnings | 0 notes` at version 0.1.0,
  and both shipped distributions are verified correct to machine
  precision against `extraDistr`.
- **The purpose of the package is to give people more distributions.**
  Everything else - the tooling for authoring new distributions - is
  secondary and does not ship in 0.1.0 (@sec-gd-scope).
- The public surface of 0.1.0 is therefore exactly two functions:
  `zero_inflated_poisson()` and `zero_inflated_negative_binomial()`.
- All 21 open issues and 6 open pull requests are grouped into **five
  milestones**, each carrying a semantic version derived from what it
  changes (@sec-gd-versioning).
- **Six issues close with the first release** ([#30](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/30), [#32](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/32), [#34](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/34), [#25](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/25), [#26](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/26),
  and the [#29](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/29) tracking issue), because the work they ask for is
  already done and verified.
- **Two of the six open PRs are already absorbed** into the current
  working tree ([#35](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/35), [#31](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/31)). The other four ([#33](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/33), [#16](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/16), [#10](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/10), [#9](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/9)) all
  predate greta 0.6.0 and **none of them has a working
  density-correctness test** - that single fact is the reason none can
  be merged as-is.

:::

## Current status {.unnumbered}

**greta.distributions** provides extra probability distributions for
greta, plus tooling for writing new ones. It has never been on CRAN.

Where things stand in July 2026:

- The package sits on branch `add-tf-zip-nb` with **uncommitted work in
  the tree**. That work took it from "will not load" to a clean check
  at 0.1.0. Nothing here is committed; every recommendation below is a
  recommendation, not an executed change.
- Two distributions ship: `zero_inflated_poisson()` and
  `zero_inflated_negative_binomial()`. Both are **verified correct**:

  ```
  ZINB greta: -1.6094379 -1.6094379 -21.0517699 -19.4523823 -16.1738951 -12.8689555
  ZINB R    : -1.6094379 -1.6094379 -21.0517699 -19.4523823 -16.1738951 -12.8689555
  max abs diff: 5.33e-15

  ZIP greta:  -1.1767850 -1.1767850  -1.5299964  -1.5299964  -3.5448994 -10.3960843
  ZIP R    :  -1.1767850 -1.1767850  -1.5299964  -1.5299964  -3.5448994 -10.3960843
  max abs diff: 8.88e-16
  ```

  (against `extraDistr::dzinb` and `extraDistr::dzip`; the test suite
  runs the same comparison over 100 random draws in
  `tests/testthat/test_zip_zinb.R:3` and `:63`.)
- Both distributions sample end-to-end under greta 0.6.0. A 50-sample,
  1-chain MCMC over 20 observations recovers sensible posteriors for
  both.
- The test suite is **8 passing tests**, up from 2.
- **Four distribution PRs are stalled at 2022-2024 vintage.** They were
  written against greta 0.4/0.5 and the `tf_distrib(parameters)`
  signature; greta 0.6.0 requires `tf_distrib(parameters, dag)` and
  batched (rank-3) tensors.

## How versions are assigned {#sec-gd-versioning}

The version comes from **what the milestone changes**, not when it ships.

greta.distributions is pre-1.0 and its public surface is small - two
distributions and four template functions - so nearly every milestone
adds capability and earns a minor bump. The one exception is milestone
1, which is a first release and takes 0.1.0 as given.

The natural 1.0 candidate is whenever the extension-author API
(milestone 4) stabilises, because that is the surface other packages
would depend on. **Not yet decided.**

## Reconciling the uncommitted work with PRs [#35](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/35) and [#31](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/31) {#sec-gd-reconcile}

This is the first thing to settle, because the uncommitted work
overlaps both PRs and the overlap is not what it looks like from the
issue titles.

### PR [#35](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/35) is not superseded - the work sits *on top of it*

The working tree is checked out on `add-tf-zip-nb`, which **is** PR
[#35](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/35)'s branch. `git diff main add-tf-zip-nb` is a single file, 14
insertions and 42 deletions, replacing the hand-written ZINB log
density with TFP's `Inflated` wrapper.

That commit, **as pushed, is broken**. It rewrote `tf_distrib` to use
`tfp$distributions$Inflated` but simultaneously *deleted the `pi`
parameter* from `initialize()`, leaving:

```r
initialize = function(size, prob, dim) {   # pi gone
  ...
  super$initialize("negative_binomial", dim, discrete = TRUE)   # wrong name
```

while the user-facing constructor still calls
`distrib("zero_inflated_negative_binomial", size, prob, pi, dim)`. The
uncommitted work repairs exactly this - restoring `pi` as a parameter,
fixing the `super$initialize()` name, and keeping the TFP `Inflated`
body (`R/zero_inflated_negative_binomial.R:34-53`).

> Claude: so the correct end state is **merge PR [#35](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/35) with the
> uncommitted repair squashed into it**, not "close [#35](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/35) as superseded".
> The PR as it stands on GitHub would ship a ZINB that ignores its own
> zero-inflation parameter. Merging it unrepaired would be worse than
> not merging it. Flagging because this is the one place where the
> obvious reading of the overlap is backwards.

### PR [#31](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/31) is superseded, but it was also never going to pass

PR [#31](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/31) adds two tests, both of which assert:

```r
expect_no_error(m <- model(example_zip))
expect_no_error(mcmc(m, n_samples = 10, warmup = 10))
```

That expectation is **impossible for a discrete distribution**, and
greta says so:

```
model(zip): ERROR: Model contains a discrete random variable that doesn't have
a fixed value, so inference cannot be carried out.
```

A zero-inflated Poisson can only ever be a likelihood for observed
data, never a free variable. PR [#31](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/31)'s tests would fail on the
`model()` line even with the underlying bug fixed. The PR correctly
identifies *what* to test (`calculate(nsim=)` works; sampling works)
and gets the *how* wrong.

The working tree now carries replacement tests that keep the intent
and fix the mechanism - asserting `calculate(nsim=)` succeeds,
asserting `model()` errors *on purpose*, and then running a real MCMC
through `distribution(y) <- ...`
(`tests/testthat/test_zip_zinb.R:18-61`). **Close [#31](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/31) as superseded.**

## Milestone 1: First CRAN release - 0.1.0

Everything needed for a first submission. This is done.

**Version: 0.1.0.** First release.

### What 0.1.0 ships, and what it deliberately does not {#sec-gd-scope}

The package exists so that greta users have access to **more
distributions**. That is the whole product for the first release. The
public surface is exactly two functions:

```
export(zero_inflated_negative_binomial)
export(zero_inflated_poisson)
```

The four distribution-authoring functions -
`greta_distribution_template()`, `greta_distribution_template_test()`,
`write_new_distribution()` and `write_distribution_test()` - **are
retained in the source but no longer exported** (`@export` became
`@noRd`). They move to @sec-gd-toolkit.

Three consequences, all of them simplifications:

- **The naming question dissolves.** PR [#33](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/33) renames those four
  functions and nothing else. With them unexported there is nothing
  public to rename, and no deprecation cycle is ever owed - they were
  never released. [#33](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/33) becomes milestone-4 work, to be settled alongside
  whatever the eventual API is.
- **The `\dontrun{}` exposure shrinks.** The blocks a first-submission
  reviewer was most likely to challenge were on
  `write_new_distribution()` and `write_distribution_test()`, which
  write files to disk. Those examples are gone from the manual, and the
  `path` argument that would have been needed to make them runnable is
  no longer required.
- **The broken template stops being a blocker.** The template generated
  code that could not run (@sec-gd-changed); that is now fixed, but it
  is no longer release-critical either way.

Issues **[#11](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/11)** (vignette on creating a new distribution) and **[#22](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/22)**
(vignette demonstrating distributions) both move out of this milestone
for the same reason - [#11](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/11) documents unexported tooling, and [#22](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/22)
documents an API that is still two distributions wide. They return when
there is more to demonstrate.

### [Issue #30](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/30)

- 2024-12-18
- zip and zinb don't work with MCMC and calculate.
- problem: `calculate(zip, nsim = 10)` failed with a TF dtype error.
- finding: **a scoping bug, not a maths bug.** `R/zero_inflated_poisson.R:62`
  read `tfp$distributions$Binomial(total_count = 1, probs = pi)`. The
  local parameter is bound as `pi_var` two lines earlier, so bare `pi`
  resolved to **base R's `pi`, 3.141593**, which reticulate marshals as
  a float64 tensor, colliding with greta's float32. Reproduced exactly
  by reverting the one identifier in an isolated copy:

  ```
  ERROR: InvalidArgumentError: cannot compute Sub as input #1(zero-based)
  was expected to be a double tensor but is a float tensor [Op:Sub]
  ```

  which is verbatim the error in the issue body.
- fix: `pi` -> `pi_var`. Already in the working tree; regression tests
  added at `tests/testthat/test_zip_zinb.R:18`.
- note: the second half of the issue ("`model(zip)` fails") is **not a
  bug** - it is greta correctly refusing to sample a free discrete
  variable. Worth saying so in the close comment.
- priority: done. **Close with the release.**

### [Issue #32](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/32)

- 2025-01-23
- tfp has zero inflated negative binomial now?
- finding: TFP 0.23.0 does expose the machinery, though the useful
  entry point is the general `tfp$distributions$Inflated`, not
  `ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial`. Confirmed present in this
  environment.
- fix: delivered by PR [#35](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/35) plus the repair in @sec-gd-reconcile. The
  ZINB is now four lines wrapping `Inflated` over `NegativeBinomial`
  (`R/zero_inflated_negative_binomial.R:47-53`) instead of ~30 lines of
  hand-rolled log density, and it matches `extraDistr::dzinb` to 5e-15.
- priority: done. **Close with the release.**

### PR [#33](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/33) - rework, then merge

- 2025-01-24, `demo-adding-new-distrib-i11`, conflicting with `main`.
- Verdict: **rework.** Three separate things are tangled in this PR.
- **(a) The API rename** - a decision, not a defect, and no longer
  urgent: the functions it renames are unexported (@sec-gd-scope), so
  no deprecation cycle is ever owed. Settle it alongside the toolkit
  API (@sec-gd-form).
- **(b) A real template bug, half-fixed.** greta's `distrib()` appends
  the suffix itself:

  ```r
  constructor <- get(x = glue::glue("{distribution}_distribution"), envir = parent.frame())
  ```

  So the generated R6 class must be named `<name>_distribution` and the
  `distrib()` call must pass the *bare* name. `main` got both wrong;
  PR [#33](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/33) fixes the class name and breaks the call. All three forms
  tested directly:

  ```
  main's template     distrib(gum, ...)                 ERROR: cannot coerce type 'environment' to vector of type 'character'
  PR #33's template   distrib('gum_distribution', ...)  ERROR: object 'gum_distribution_distribution' not found
  correct             distrib('gum', ...)               worked
  ```

  **Fixed in the working tree** (`R/distribution-template.R:8-9` and
  `:178`). A generated template now round-trips: filling in only the
  placeholders the template itself marks yields a working distribution
  whose node class is `gumbel_distribution`.
- **(c) The vignette** - keep, but it documents unexported tooling now,
  so it rebases onto whatever the toolkit API becomes.
- priority: **downgraded to milestone 4.** With the authoring functions
  unexported (@sec-gd-scope), all three strands of this PR are about
  code that does not ship in 0.1.0. The template bug (b) is already
  fixed in the working tree regardless; (a) and (c) wait for
  @sec-gd-toolkit.

## Milestone 2: The stalled distribution PRs - 0.2.0 {#sec-gd-prs}

Land the four distributions that have been sitting in open PRs since
2022. They are grouped together because they share one blocker and one
gap.

**Version: 0.2.0 (minor).** Adds distributions.

**The shared blocker.** All three PRs were written against the
`tf_distrib = function(parameters)` signature. greta 0.6.0 passes
`dag` as a second argument, so every one of them fails at
construction:

```
Error in `distrib_constructor(tf_parameter_list, dag = self)`: unused argument (dag = self)
```

That part is a one-line fix per file. The harder part is that greta
0.6.0 batches tensors to rank 3, and the multivariate distributions
([#9](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/9), [#10](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/10)) hit `tf$tile`:

```
Expected multiples argument to be a vector of length 3 but got length 2 [Op:Tile]
```

**The shared gap.** *None of the three PRs has a working
density-correctness test.* In every case the `compare_distribution()`
block is commented out:

- `tests/testthat/test-conditional_bernoulli.R:1-10` - commented, and
  the stub compares against `stats::dnorm`, which is not the
  distribution.
- `tests/testthat/test-multivariate-probit.R:6-15` - commented.
- `tests/testthat/test-discrete_lognormal.R:17-42` - both blocks
  commented, and the stubs reference `extraDistr::rzinb` for a
  discrete *normal*.

What passes in those PRs is argument-validation snapshot tests only
(PR [#9](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/9)'s 6 green tests are all `expect_snapshot_error` on bad
dimensions). **No reviewer should merge a distribution whose density
has never been checked against a reference.** Each of these needs a
`compare_distribution()` block before it lands - which is exactly what
the shipped ZIP/ZINB have.

### PR [#16](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/16) - split it; half works

- 2022-07-27, `hrlai/main` (fork, Lai Hao Ran), conflicting, marked
  draft by the author.
- Verdict: **rework, and split into two.**
- `discrete_normal()` **works end to end.** Constructed, attached as a
  likelihood over binned data, and sampled: 50-sample MCMC on
  `mean`/`sd` completed without error under greta 0.6.0. It already
  uses the modern `tf_distrib(parameters, dag)` signature
  (`R/discrete_normal.R:85`).
- `discrete_lognormal()` **is broken, and always was.** It calls a
  4-argument helper with 2 arguments:

  ```
  R/tf_functions.R:4       tf_safe_cdf <- function(x, distribution, lower_bound, upper_bound)
  R/discrete_lognormal.R:84  low <- tf_safe_cdf(tf_lower_vec, d)
  ```

  Constructing and attaching it succeeds; MCMC fails with
  `RuntimeError: argument "lower_bound" is missing, with no default`.
  `discrete_normal.R:115-116` passes all four correctly, which is why
  it works - the bug is confined to the lognormal.
- Also: the two have **inconsistent signatures** -
  `discrete_normal(mean, sd, breaks, edges, dim)` versus
  `discrete_lognormal(meanlog, sdlog, breaks, dim)`. One of them
  should lose or gain `edges`.
- Also: the PR adds `R/conda_greta_env.R`, which is dead - greta 0.6.0
  replaced conda with `uv`. Drop it.
- fix: merge `discrete_normal` first with a density test; fix
  `tf_safe_cdf` arity and reconcile the signature before merging
  `discrete_lognormal`.
- Resolves [#7](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/7).
- priority: high - it is the closest of the three to done, and the
  author is an outside contributor whose draft has been open since
  2022.

> Claude: PR [#16](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/16) is from a fork and has been open three and a half
> years. Whatever the verdict, it probably deserves a comment saying
> so. `discrete_normal` working is genuinely good news and worth
> telling the author.

### PR [#9](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/9) - rework, moderate

- 2022-06-10, `add-conditional-bernouilli`, conflicting.
- Verdict: **rework.**
- The signature fix is one line (`R/conditional-bernoulli.R:94`).
  After it, the distribution constructs and attaches as a likelihood
  successfully.
- `calculate(nsim=)` then gives a clean, honest greta error -
  `Sampling is not yet implemented for "conditional_bernoulli"` -
  because `sample = NULL` (`R/conditional-bernoulli.R:119`). So PR [#9](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/9)'s
  own `test-calculate-distribution.R` assertion cannot pass; either
  write a `sample` method or drop that test.
- The remaining blocker is the rank-3 batching: evaluating the density
  through greta 0.6.0's dag hits the `tf$tile` error above. This is
  real work, not a signature tweak.
- Resolves [#5](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/5) and [#27](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/27) (duplicates of each other).
- priority: medium.

### PR [#10](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/10) - rework, substantial

- 2022-06-10, `add-multivariate-probit-i6`, conflicting.
- Verdict: **rework - the most incomplete of the four.**
- Same signature fix (`R/multivariate-probit.R:88`); after it,
  construction succeeds.
- But attaching it as a likelihood fails on its own dimension check:
  `mean must be a 2D greta array with one column, but has dimensions 1 x 2`.
  Its own test file passes `matrix(rnorm(2), nrow = 2)` for `mean`
  while the docs describe `mean` per-realisation - the intended shape
  contract is not settled.
- Its only non-commented test fails: `calculate(mp, nsim = 1)` gives
  *the target greta_arrays are related to variables that do not have
  distributions so cannot be sampled*.
- Resolves [#6](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/6).
- priority: low - most work, least settled design.

### [Issue #28](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/28)

- 2018-10-04
- possible typo in conditional_bernoulli docs.
- finding: **the reporter is right, and the bug is still there in PR
  [#9](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/9).** The docs give the density as

  ```
  psi * prod((p ^ y) * (1 - p) ^ (1 - y)) + max(y) * (1 - psi)
  ```

  (`R/conditional-bernoulli.R:23`) but the code computes

  ```r
  none <- tf_as_float(tf_rowsums(x, 1L) == 0)      # 1 iff all y are 0
  prob <- exp(tf_rowsums(log_cp, 1L) + log(psi)) + none * (one - psi)
  ```

  (`R/conditional-bernoulli.R:103, :114`). `none` is `1 - max(y)` for
  binary `y` - the opposite of the doc. The code is correct: under the
  MacKenzie occupancy formulation the "absent" term contributes only
  when the species was never detected. The documentation is wrong.
- fix: `max(y)` -> `(1 - max(y))` in the roxygen `\deqn`. One word.
- caveat: I could not evaluate the density numerically to confirm,
  because the distribution does not run under greta 0.6.0's batching
  (the `tf$tile` blocker above). The finding rests on reading an
  unambiguous expression, not on execution. **Re-verify once PR [#9](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/9) is
  reworked.**
- priority: low, but free - ships with PR [#9](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/9).

### Issues [#5](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/5), [#6](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/6), [#7](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/7), [#27](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/27)

- These are the feature requests the three PRs implement: [#5](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/5)/#27
  conditional bernoulli, [#6](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/6) multivariate probit, [#7](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/7) discrete
  lognormal/normal.
- [#5](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/5) (2022-06-10) and [#27](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/27) (2017-11-02) are **duplicates**; [#27](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/27) is the
  original and has the fuller derivation. Keep [#27](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/27), close [#5](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/5) as a
  duplicate, or vice versa - but not both.
- Each closes when its PR lands.

## Milestone 3: The zero-inflation and hurdle family - 0.3.0

Generalise what the ZINB rewrite proved: `tfp$distributions$Inflated`
turns any base distribution into a zero-inflated one in four lines.
That makes most of this milestone cheap.

**Version: 0.3.0 (minor).** Adds distributions.

### [Issue #20](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/20)

- 2024-02-12
- hurdles and zero inflated distributions.
- finding: this is the **design issue that should be settled before
  [#21](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/21) and [#18](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/18) are coded**, because it names the distinction: zero
  inflation is a point mass *plus* a distribution that may already
  contain zeros; a hurdle is a point mass *plus a truncated*
  distribution. TFP's `Inflated` gives the first directly. The second
  needs a truncation layer greta.distributions does not have.
- fix: decide the interface for both, then implement.
- priority: high - it gates the rest of the milestone.

### [Issue #21](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/21)

- 2024-08-20
- Add zero inflated beta distribution.
- finding: with `Inflated` established, this is the ZINB pattern over
  `tfp$distributions$Beta`. Note it is *zero*-inflated beta, so the
  support is [0,1) - a continuous distribution with a point mass, which
  unlike ZIP/ZINB **can** be a free variable.
- fix: four lines plus a density test.
- priority: medium. ("For biocrust modelling by August" - that August
  has passed; worth asking if the need is live.)

### [Issue #18](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/18)

- 2023-05-16
- add Tweedie distribution.
- finding: the requester (hrlai, same contributor as PR [#16](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/16)) points at
  an upstream TFP PR. Needs checking whether it ever landed in TFP
  0.23.0 - if not, this is a hand-written log density, which is a much
  larger job than [#21](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/21).
- priority: low.

### [Issue #14](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/14)

- 2022-06-16
- add ordered_logit distribution.
- finding: TFP has `OrderedLogistic`, so this is a wrapper. **Overlaps
  greta issue [#264](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/264)**, which lists the same distribution in greta's own
  milestone 5. One of the two packages should own it.
- priority: medium.

> Claude: [#14](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/14) here and [greta
> [#264](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/264)](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/264) are the same
> distribution. More generally, greta's milestone 5 and this package
> both claim "new distributions". **Where is the line?** My assumption
> throughout has been: greta ships the standard catalogue, and
> greta.distributions ships the specialist and compound ones. If that
> is right, ordered logit belongs *here* and greta [#264](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/264) should close
> pointing at [#14](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/14).

### [Issue #19](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/19)

- 2024-02-08
- Some more distributions to implement.
- finding: a **backlog list**, not an actionable issue - it points at
  glmmTMB's and gamlss's catalogues. The genuinely useful content is
  the pointer to `gamlss.tr` for generic truncation, which is the
  machinery [#20](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/20) needs for hurdles.
- fix: keep as the milestone's parking lot; file specific issues off
  it as they get picked up.
- priority: low, never closes on its own.

## Milestone 4: The extension-author toolkit - 0.4.0 {#sec-gd-toolkit}

Make "write your own greta distribution" a supported workflow rather
than a copy-paste exercise. **This is where the four authoring
functions now live**, unexported since 0.1.0 (@sec-gd-scope), together
with everything that documents or renames them: issue **[#11](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/11)** (the
authoring vignette) and PR **[#33](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/33)** (the API rename plus that vignette).

**Version: 0.4.0 (minor).** Adds and stabilises public API.

### Did we arrive at a good form? No {#sec-gd-form}

The template functions were repaired this July so that they *generate
code that runs* (@sec-gd-changed). That is not the same as the API
being right, and four things say it is not:

**It is a string-interpolating code generator.**
`build_greta_dist_definition()` glues R6 source together as text:

```{r}
#| eval: false
top <- glue::glue(
  '{dist_name}_distribution <- R6::R6Class(
       classname = "{dist_name}_distribution",
```

The class-name/`distrib()` contract therefore lives in string
concatenation, where nothing can check it - which is exactly why
`main`'s template and PR [#33](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/33)'s template got it wrong in **two
different ways**. Two independent attempts failing differently is a
statement about the design, not about the authors.

**The signature is too thin for the job.** `dist_arg_list =
c("meanlog", "sdlog")` carries names and nothing else. A distribution
also needs parameter constraints (positive? simplex? correlation?),
support and truncation, discrete versus continuous, dimension rules,
the TFP distribution to delegate to, and the bijector. None of that is
expressible, so the generated file is a skeleton whose hard parts are
all left to the author.

**The generated code walks into [#12](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/12).** Emitted code calls greta
functions bare, and inside a package namespace `beta(1, 1)` silently
returns numeric `1` (see [#12](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/12) above). A generator should emit `greta::`
prefixes, or [#12](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/12) should be fixed first.

**The vignette is the product, not the function.** For a "help people
author distributions" feature, [#11](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/11) *is* the deliverable and the
functions are scaffolding around it. Shipping the scaffolding first was
backwards.

### The form that issue [#4](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/4) already describes

Golding's sketch in [#4](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/4) - `write_greta_distribution(name=, arguments=,
tf_distrib_name=, truncation=, tf_distrib_args=)` - is a **declarative
specification**, not a code generator. Describe the distribution as
data, and have one function construct the node from it. Then there is
no generated source to get wrong, the spec can be validated, and a
density can be tested without first writing a file to disk.

The gap between that sketch and the shipped implementation is the real
content of this milestone.

### This is the same problem as greta [#369](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/369) {#sec-gd-369}

greta's own [#369](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/369),
"helpers to establish new TFP/greta distributions", sits in greta's
milestone 9. It asks the same question this milestone asks. It is also
the same *shape* as greta's milestone 8 - replacing stringly-typed
machinery with declarative descriptions, one level up.

**Designing this toolkit separately from [#369](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/369) risks building two
competing answers to one question.** The recommendation is to treat
them as one piece of design work, and to schedule this milestone
against [#369](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/369) rather than ahead of it.

> Claude: this also bears on the backend endgame. A declarative spec
> that names a TFP distribution is portable to another backend only if
> the naming is indirected; a spec that composes greta ops is portable
> for free. Worth settling alongside greta's `compose where cheap,
> delegate where not` default.

### [Issue #12](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/12)

- 2022-06-10
- How to best reexport greta internals.
- finding: **this is a real trap and I hit it while writing tests.**
  `R/internals.R` pulls greta internals into the package namespace, but
  greta itself is in `Depends`, not `Imports`. R's namespace search
  goes *namespace -> imports -> base -> global -> search path*, so
  `base` is reached **before** the attached greta. Inside the package
  namespace, and inside its tests, `beta(1, 1)` therefore resolves to
  `base::beta` and returns the numeric `1`, not a greta array:

  ```
  Error in `model(size, prob, pi)`: `model()` arguments must be <greta_array>s
  The following objects passed to `model()` are not <greta array>s: "prob" and "pi"
  ```

  I worked around it with `greta::beta(1, 1)` in
  `tests/testthat/test_zip_zinb.R:33, :54-55`, but the workaround is
  the evidence: any distribution author writing code *inside* a package
  that depends on greta hits the same silent masking.
- fix: move greta to `Imports` and re-export what authors need
  explicitly, which is what the issue proposes. That also answers the
  issue's discomfort about documenting re-exported internals - a small
  documented surface (`distrib`, `distribution_node`, `check_dims`,
  `fl`, `as.greta_array`) is defensible where `.internals` is not.
- priority: high within this milestone; it is the difference between
  the templates working for the package and working for its users.

### [Issue #4](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/4)

- 2022-06-10
- some notes on interface design.
- finding: the **design charter for the whole template system** -
  Golding's sketch of `write_greta_distribution(name=, arguments=,
  tf_distrib_name=, truncation=, tf_distrib_args=)`. The shipped
  `greta_distribution_template()` implements a weaker version: it takes
  a name and an argument list but not the TFP mapping, so the generated
  `tf_distrib` body is a commented placeholder the author fills in.
- fix: close the gap between the sketch and the implementation, or
  record the decision not to.
- priority: medium. It is the issue that says what "done" means for
  this package's second half.

> Claude: [#4](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/4) is eight years of unrealised design and the templates now
> half-implement it. **Is the `tf_distrib_name`/`tf_distrib_args`
> mapping still wanted?** If yes, this milestone is the place. If the
> answer is "the placeholder approach is fine, authors need to think
> about the density anyway", then [#4](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/4) closes and the milestone shrinks
> to [#12](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/12).

## Milestone 5: Sufficient statistics - 0.5.0

**Version: 0.5.0 (minor).** New capability, no API break.

### [Issue #37](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/37)

- 2026-02-10
- Explore using sufficient statistics to speed up models.
- finding: the newest issue and the only performance one. Points at
  Jewson et al. (arXiv 2502.04990) and Stan implementations that
  rewrite a Gaussian regression likelihood in terms of sufficient
  statistics, turning an O(n) density into O(1) in the data.
- finding: this is **research, not a distribution.** It also sits
  awkwardly here: the rewrite is a property of the *model graph*, which
  is greta's business, not a property of a distribution. It may belong
  in greta's milestone 8/9 (graph rewriting) rather than in this
  package.
- fix: prototype on one model - Bayesian linear regression - and
  measure before designing anything.
- priority: low.

> Claude: **I think [#37](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/37) is filed in the wrong repository.** Marginalisation
> and decentring in greta's milestone 9 are the same shape of problem -
> rewrite the graph, preserve the posterior - and they need the flat
> node registry from greta's milestone 8. Moving [#37](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/37) to greta would put
> it with its machinery. Your call, but I would not build it here.

## What I changed {#sec-gd-changed}

All in the working tree, uncommitted, on branch `add-tf-zip-nb`. The
package checks `0 errors | 0 warnings | 0 notes` at 0.1.0 after every
change, and the test suite went from 2 tests to 8, all passing.

| File | Change | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `R/distribution-template.R:8-9` | Generated R6 class renamed `<name>_distribution` | `distrib()` appends the suffix; without this the constructor lookup fails |
| `R/distribution-template.R:174-183` | `distrib([name], ...)` -> `distrib("[name]", ...)`, outer string requoted to single quotes | all three call forms tested; only this one works |
| `R/greta_distribution_template_test.R:25, :28` | `extraDist::` -> `extraDistr::` | the package is `extraDistr`; `extraDist` does not exist |
| `tests/testthat/test_zip_zinb.R:18-61` | Two regression tests for [#30](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/30), replacing PR [#31](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/31)'s | 8/8 tests pass; supersedes PR [#31](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/31) |

Everything else in the tree is the previous agent's work, left intact.

## The path to a first CRAN release

Narrowing 0.1.0 to the two distributions (@sec-gd-scope) removed the
three items that used to head this list - the naming decision, the [#33](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/33)
rework, and the [#11](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/11) vignette. What remains:

1. **Squash the working-tree repair into PR [#35](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/35) and merge it.** Do not
   merge [#35](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/35) unrepaired (@sec-gd-reconcile).
2. **Close [#31](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/31)** as superseded.
3. **Close [#30](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/30), [#32](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/32), [#34](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/34), [#25](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/25), [#26](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/26)** - all verified done above.
4. **Amend [#29](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/29)'s checklist**, which still lists [#11](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/11) and [#22](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/22) as release
   requirements. Both moved out (@sec-gd-toolkit, @sec-gd-prs).
5. **Move [#33](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/33) to milestone 4** - it renames unexported functions, so it
   no longer touches the release.
6. Run the [#29](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.distributions/issues/29) checklist tail: `urlchecker::url_check()`,
   `devtools::check(remote = TRUE, manual = TRUE)`,
   `check_win_devel()`, then submit.

Two notes on the submission itself. `cran-comments.md` was written when
the authoring functions were still exported, so **its `\dontrun{}`
justification now covers examples that no longer exist** - it needs
trimming to match. And the largest remaining risk is unchanged: nothing
here has been demonstrated on a machine *without* Python, which is what
CRAN has. `check_win_devel()` and rhub are not optional.

Milestones 2 onward are all post-release. Nothing in them blocks 0.1.0,
and **none of the four legacy PRs should be rushed into the first
release** - they would each add a distribution whose density has never
been compared against a reference, to a package whose entire credibility
rests on its densities being right.
